review_note: Judge's 410 AAA PA, 19 HR and 98 K contrast with 42 K in just 95 MLB PA; scouting rank .70 is present. Common centering raises conditional hitting only from -.040 to .107 while PA stays 281.5, far from 678 and 52 HR next year. The direct tree gives scouting a positive .296/.262 path contribution, but its total offense falls to about .55/.56. The actual 8.372 remains the largest false low in every alternative. Cowart/Gose peers did not have Judge's breakout, and Pinder improved much less. This is compressed elite-entry evidence and genuinely extreme growth, not a replacement-reference problem or justification for boosting every brief debut.

The 62-HR, 696-PA season follows 39 HR in 633 PA. Hitting is already regressed considerably: 3.259 baseline versus 5.312 realized per 600. Common centering reduces it to 3.155, and direct offense drops to 3.942/3.748 versus 5.489 actual. The saved fits rely heavily on pooled MLB quality; common rate also replaces workload/calendar coefficients, including a -.185 extra reorganization contribution. PA stays 507 versus 458 actual, so the deterioration is not caused by less opportunity. Only one distinct matching narrow profile exists; ordinary age/workload peers are not comparable power extremes.

The source already includes 62, 37 and 58 HR in the preceding three MLB years. Baseline rate 4.534 falls to 4.247, with the common model's reorganization term -.647 versus -.266 baseline explaining a substantial part of the fitted difference, not a causal rule. Direct heads reduce 5.666 offense to 5.186/4.887, while actual is 9.393 in 679 PA. The unchanged 531 PA also understates use. No player occupies the exact narrow stage/age/workload/quality profile; generic established peers have much weaker power. This is not evidence that stars should never regress, but these replacements worsen an already compressed star forecast.

Winn has 498 AAA PA with 18 HR and 83 K before a 137-PA MLB debut. His common rate improves from -.769 to -.640; total offense rises from .608 to .680, with direct heads .666/.776 versus 1.741 actual. All retain only 335 expected PA against 637. Tree terms show upper-minor role, roster and scouting evidence reaching the fit; missing data is not the explanation. Carter and Paris peers fail more strongly, Butler breaks out and Crow-Armstrong receives playing time without much offense. Positive entry evidence is useful but not a guaranteed full season, and this batting test cannot repair the unchanged opportunity gap.

Steer's 2022 AA/AAA totals contain 23 HR in 492 PA before 108 MLB PA. The direct heads respond positively to AAA role and AA/AAA HR, but yield about .62 offense rather than .675 baseline and 4.801 actual. Common rate also moves the wrong way, -.212 to -.298, partly through the calendar coefficient. PA stays 243 versus 665, so none is a new solution to readiness/use. Wallner succeeds among the origin-selected peers, while Burdick and Stowers receive little use. Coarse support is available; useful upper-minor production was present but the fitted effect is too weak for this particular fast progression.

A blank current MLB season follows 403 MLB PA and earlier strong AAA production. Common rate drops .251 to -.074, largely with a -.376 additional calendar term, and offense falls .615 to .521. Direct heads instead value prior MLB quality and role, raising offense to 1.870/1.812. Actual return is 577 PA but -1.140 batting per 600 and .706 offense. The baseline's close value is cancellation of too little PA with too optimistic hitting, not an accurate recovery forecast. Direct improvement in recognizing old quality does not mean it correctly predicted the return's performance. Narrow profiles have six active or fifteen all-outcome people; all four generic inactive peers do not return.

Tatis's source contains 42 HR in 546 MLB PA in 2021 and 17 in 257 during 2020, then only fourteen AA PA in the blank MLB year. The direct trees use pooled MLB quality plus younger age and past role to lift offense from .184 to 2.787/2.522, closer to 3.333 actual. This is the largest gain, not a newly predicted 635 PA: baseline PA remains 34.8. The direct totals are mathematically within the extreme event envelope but imply exceptional offensive yield relative to that tiny use, so they cannot be advertised as a normal coherent talent/workload decomposition. Generic absent peers are failed fringe players, not comparable former stars; their zero outcomes do not settle Tatis's return risk.

The actual inputs contain the fourth overall pick, known 4YR JR class, college indicator and zero elapsed draft years, plus four HR, seven K and ten walks in 35 A PA and fifteen AA PA. No new college collection is needed to see this evidence. All forecasts nearly miss the next-year 489 PA, 36 HR and 5.838 offense: baseline PA is two, and direct offense .0027/.0001. Preseason scouting rank is absent because he had only just been drafted, not a zero pedigree. Thousands of generic upper-minor no-debut profiles are not elite recent-college-entry support. Cam Smith and Christian Moore enter among peers while Montgomery/Williams do not. This is a real readiness/representation weakness, not solved by common target units.

Fourth-pick college pedigree and 200 actual minor PA spanning complex through AAA are present. Common rate rises .688 to .785, but future rate is only .077; that change is not better talent prediction. Direct value rises .183 to .365/.332 versus 1.796 actual, principally through upper-minor role and HR terms. PA remains 43 against 557. Crews enters modestly while Veen, Shaw and Wilken do not enter the next year. Unlike Kurtz he has meaningful upper-minor exposure, but neither head handles the fast college pathway satisfactorily. Long-term prospect quality must not be equated with the same immediate PA for every top pick.

At eighteen Soto has eight K and three HR in 96 A PA, plus earlier complex production. The actual pooled lower-level inputs exist; common rate improves .252 to .349, with low-K terms positive, but conditional training support in the narrow profile is only eight people. Expected PA stays .129; direct values also remain near zero against 494 PA, 22 HR and 4.111 actual. Thousands of mostly zero direct-outcome profiles do not identify rare immediate stars. Every generic young lower-minor peer has zero next-year MLB PA. This is an exceptional fast-arrival miss that remains unresolved, not evidence that Soto lacked talent or that all low-level players deserve immediate MLB jobs.

Alvarez has 37 HR, 106 K and 69 unintentional walks in 561 current PA following 33 HR in 598. The saved quality terms are strongly positive, but common rate declines 2.814 to 2.731 versus 5.273 actual. Direct values fall 4.001 to 3.863/3.606 versus 5.912. PA is already close, 512 against 496, so this is a talent/value deterioration rather than opportunity improvement. Nine distinct narrow-profile people warn against treating generic age/use peers as true superstar analogs. Devers/Arraez/Torres outcomes are mixed but generally positive; none justifies this alternative's extra compression of Alvarez.

With 635 PA, 35 HR and 95 K in the current year, baseline forecast 554 PA and 5.186 offense is defensible from known use but misses the actual 199 PA and .973 offense. Common rate reduces 3.746 to 3.471 and value to 4.932, the largest squared-error gain for that arm. Its extra negative calendar term is about -.376; this is not knowledge of the later lost playing time. Both direct heads remain above five or nearly five. Devers and Torres perform well among peers while De La Cruz barely plays. This favorable error reduction is not a validated health forecast or a reason to reduce all strong hitters.

Davis still has 26 HR in 524 PA, but K rise to 195 after 219/208 in the preceding years. Baseline PA 507 is close to actual 522; batting is the failure, 1.082 predicted versus -4.102 realized. Common centering increases it to 1.451 and offense 2.784 versus -1.963 actual, the largest harm/false high for that arm. Exact changes include career exposure, draft elapsed and K coefficients rather than learning impending collapse. The direct common head also overstates him more. Several older-use peers decline, though Duda is less severe. This is a performance-collapse miss and a bad replacement tradeoff, not a workload bug or proof every veteran decline was predictable.

Hicks's source has 126 current PA, four HR and thirty K after 211 short-season PA and 255 in 2019. Common offense .523 almost exactly matches .521 realized, but expected PA is 197 versus 453 and batting -.291 versus -1.190. The apparent ordinary value success is cancellation of serious workload and rate errors. Direct heads .808/.701 are farther away. Saved common-rate changes redistribute prior work/exposure terms and do not repair actual PA. Peers include little-use or poor-output Plawecki, Piscotty and Hamilton, plus diminished Rendon. A good final number alone is not confirmation of health or true hitting ability.

Bichette has 601/697/690 recent MLB PA and 20/24/29 HR, so positive future output is sensible from known evidence. Direct trees amplify pooled quality, role and age to 4.317/4.402 offense versus 3.436 baseline; actual is -.480 in 336 PA. Both conditional common rate and direct value worsen the miss. The result-selected case diagnoses over-optimistic delivered output, not foreknowledge of his later collapse. Peña and Steer play substantial seasons among origin-selected peers, while Melendez and Varsho deliver less offense. Broad support exists, but the fitted aggregate loss did not protect against this major false high.

Azócar has 343 AA and 201 AAA PA in 2021; no HR and only six walks in the AAA sample. Direct relative offense .01295 matches .01289 actual, but retained PA is 12.7 versus 216 and baseline conditional rate -1.047 versus -1.844 realized. Saved tree terms use AAA role positively and low AAA walks negatively; the very low total is not an accurate workload projection. The perfect value reflects little net offense in substantial realized use. Stefanic also enters, Casey and Beltre do not, and Larsen gets one PA. Preserve the distinction between predicting a low-value hitter and predicting he will scarcely play.

Salas's high preseason rank .93 coexists with four HR and 98 K in 469 A+ PA at eighteen. The direct tree assigns the rank about +1.144/+1.109 offense wins, leading to 1.155/1.176 expected offense despite unchanged expected PA 7.224. The physical maximum on the fixed event scale is only 1.042 even if every expected PA had the most valuable outcome. The pair is therefore incoherent, not a high confidence prospect value. Actual next-year MLB PA is zero, with no observed hitting rate. Generic peers also do not arrive but lack his elite rank. The comparison reveals failed integration of pedigree and immediate readiness, not evidence against his eventual talent.

Seager has 613 current PA with 22 HR and sixty-two walks, following 687 PA and 26 HR. Direct common offense rises 3.720 baseline to 4.948, principally through pooled quality and recent MLB workload/role paths. Actual falls to .368 in 115 PA; this is the largest direct-common deterioration. Nothing in this isolated batting comparison forecasts later injury, and unchanged PA 624 remains badly high. Gallo and Benintendi have substantial positive seasons among the origin-selected peers; Anderson's hitting is modest. A favorable young established profile can still lose availability, and a better joint architecture must handle that risk rather than merely amplify good histories.

Torrens has 130/30/166 recent MLB PA, plus current 124 AAA PA with five HR. Common direct offense .148 matches .147 actual almost perfectly through positive AAA HR and roster terms offset by weak pooled MLB quality and role. Yet PA stays 120 versus 283, and the direct model supplies no conditional talent forecast. Baseline hitting -1.407 is near -1.561 actual; common-rate replacement makes it -1.680. Herrera plays among the peers while Olivares does not and Stefanic/Sánchez get little use. This ordinary final-value match is not proof that the direct architecture provides correct playing time or a complete catcher/defensive value model.
